data.narrative:
Terran Robotics is a seed-stage robotics and manufacturing company founded by Zach Dwiel and Danny Weddle that has raised $256K to date. The valuation universe comprises 9 private peers in robotics and manufacturing (including Walden Robotics, Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, and Generalist AI) plus 1 public comparable (277810.KQ).

The applicable valuation method is stage-progression analysis. Using total capital raised ($256K) as a baseline proxy and applying a typical 2.5x step-up multiplier from seed to the next financing stage yields $640K. A peer-median approach was not feasible; while 10 same-sector peers exist in the robotics and manufacturing universe, none of the narrow filters—same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-valuation-tier comparable—produced three or more datapoints. Relying on an all-sector median would introduce unacceptable distortion.

The triangulation supports a valuation range of $544K to $736K, with a median estimate of $640K. This analysis is constrained by reliance on a single method and the absence of a robust peer set at the seed stage. Key uncertainties include the applicability of the 2.5x multiplier to this specific team and market, capital efficiency relative to robotics sector norms, and near-term funding prospects that could shift valuation dynamics. Additional diligence on comparable seed rounds in robotics would materially strengthen conviction in this range.
